newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Dutch welcome widest possible EMU membership.
newsitem.headline: Dutch welcome widest possible EMU membership.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo said on Monday that as many states as possible should join Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), provided they meet tough entry criteria.
Asked to comment on a report that his cabinet colleague, Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm, doubted Portugal would be among those launching the single currency, Van Mierlo said:

"The position of the Dutch cabinet, including the prime minister, the minister of foreign affairs and the minister of finance, is that each country which meets the criteria is welcome in the EMU and the more there are, the better it is."
"That has always been the position and we have never intended to change that," Van Mierlo told a news conference.
Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama, also present, said Portugal would be ready to join when the single currency starts in 1998.
"In 1998 countries will be judged by the individual achievements of the economies, and that is what matters. We are preparing to join in the first stage," he said.

Last week Portuguese newspaper Diario Economico quoted Zalm, who will chair meetings of EU finance ministers for the next six months, as saying he was sceptical about Lisbon's chances of qualifying in the first wave of countries.
